quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should not be used unless the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing in orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you NOT do to improve your safety when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when other vehicles are not nearby, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you—their headlights show the road ahead, and their taillights show if there are bumps in the road.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Roll on the throttle.
Hold the handgrips loosely.
Gently apply the brake of the non-flat tire.
Increase your speed to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the non-flat tire.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and stay in a straight line as you slow down. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip.
Near the right handgrip.
Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip.
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: For eye and face shield protection to work well, it must have all of these features EXCEPT:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be too tight to wear sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if you need them.

questions.question: The best sitting position when riding:

options.text: Requires your arms to hold you up.
Allows you to easily reach the controls.
Keeps your arms straight when reaching the handgrips.
Keeps your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
More difficult than braking on a straight road.
Safe to do with only the front brake.
Safe to do with only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you need proper technique and great care.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Position yourself where the car driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Do not worry about your position.
Always ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself where the car driver can see you.
questions.explanation: When riding directly behind a car, ride in the center of your lane. This position is most visible in the car's rearview mirror. Drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the side of the road and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of the lane in wet conditions. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. The left tire track is often the best choice, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the mirrors are clean.
Check that the horn works.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is open, not closed.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Move side to side across your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: To prevent other cars from trying to share your lane, ride in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you feel tired while riding.
When you will slow down where drivers do not expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals are broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where drivers do not expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, such as the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if you can.
Stay seated and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: How do you get maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straightaway, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is one benefit of doing regular maintenance on your motorcycle?

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance will take a lot of time.
Maintenance will be expensive.
Maintenance checks help prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Make regular maintenance inspections part of your routine care.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Lean when you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when you lean. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What should you NOT check during your pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, inspect your motorcycle carefully. Check the tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What should passengers do on a motorcycle?

options.text: Lean with the operator.
Never come into contact with the operator.
Sit as far back on their seat as possible.
Hold onto their seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other traffic happens at intersections. Stay alert where another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, usually just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.
